name: Domperidone
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Nausea and vomiting (adults and adolescents 12 years and older, 35 kg or more)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 10 mg up to three times daily, before meals; maximum 30 mg/day; usually no longer than 1 week

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir and other protease inhibitors)
key_interactions.effect: Higher domperidone levels and QT prolongation.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: QT-prolonging drugs (class IA and III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics, antidepressants, antibiotics, antimalarials)
key_interactions.action: Contraindicated (apomorphine only under its SmPC conditions).

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (diltiazem, verapamil, some macrolides)
Drugs causing bradycardia or hypokalemia; azithromycin, roxithromycin
key_interactions.action: Use with caution; monitor ECG and potassium.
Do not take at the same time.

serious: QTc prolongation, torsades de pointes, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death
Extrapyramidal reactions, convulsions (mainly in overdose and young children)

contraindications: QTc or other conduction prolongation, significant electrolyte disturbance, or heart disease such as heart failure
Co-administration with QT-prolonging drugs or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
monitoring: QTc and electrolytes in at-risk patients (age over 60, heart disease, kidney failure, interacting drugs)
Limit to 30 mg/day and the shortest course

pk.half_life_eskd: Rises from 7.4 to 20.8 hours at CrCl <30 mL/min/1.73 m2
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 31% of dose in urine (about 1% unchanged); 66% in feces
